signatures.description: Implement a Hybrid Logical Clock (48-bit physical milliseconds packed with a 16-bit logical counter) with serialize/deserialize, plus a causal-broadcast layer that delivers a message only after its full dependency set has been observed, buffering out-of-order messages and flushing them in deterministic timestamp order. The clock must stay strictly monotonic when the wall clock jumps backwards (an NTP correction), and a deserialized remote timestamp that exceeds the configured max drift must be rejected or clamped without ever letting this node emit a timestamp that compares less than one it already emitted. Verify with a property-based simulator that randomly partitions, delays, duplicates and reorders a lossy network, asserting exactly-once delivery, per-node monotonicity of emitted timestamps, and that no message is ever delivered before all of its causal dependencies.
